History:
- Presenting complaint: Lip swelling starting at the left corner of the upper lip after consuming prawn-containing food; swelling is enlarging and ongoing.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began about 7:00 pm, developed over ~30 minutes; continuing to worsen.
- Associated symptoms/context: Sensation of throat closing and difficulty breathing; chest tightness uncertain; dizziness. Had prior similar swelling after a late-night meal (curry) in childhood with breathing difficulty.
- Triggers: Prawn-containing dish; history of food-related allergies (peanut allergy).
- Relevant history: Asthma; uses Salbutamol inhaler; peanut allergy with past suspected severe allergic reaction in childhood.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Asthma.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy.
- Medications: Salbutamol (inhaler) used regularly; antihistamine use not clearly documented.
- Prior hospitalizations: None documented; history of a severe allergic reaction at around age 6.

Physical Examination:
- Findings reported by patient: Lip swelling on the upper lip; swelling enlarging; sensation of throat tightness; shortness of breath/difficulty breathing; dizziness.
- No other physical exam details or vitals provided in transcript.

Impression:
- Suspected anaphylactic reaction to prawn with airway involvement (throat/chest symptoms and progressive swelling).

Management Plan:
- Immediate actions: Ambulance to be called and arrival coordinated; accompanied by someone if possible; take antihistamines in the meantime if available.
- Safety instructions: Have someone with you until EMS arrives; relay to dispatcher that suspected anaphylaxis is occurring.
- Follow-up: After hospital, contact the clinic again as there may be a need to arrange injections and further allergy management.

Patient Summary:
- Maria Trabalotsa, with asthma and peanut allergy, developed rapidly progressive lip swelling after prawn soup, with throat tightening and breathing difficulties. Suspected anaphylaxis; ambulance arranged; advised to go to hospital and follow up for possible injections and allergy management.

Key Takeaways:
- Recognize signs of possible anaphylaxis (airway involvement, swelling, breathing difficulties) and seek emergency help immediately.
- Use available antihistamines if present while awaiting EMS; ensure someone is with you; go to the emergency department for urgent evaluation and treatment.

Next Steps:
- Proceed to emergency care now.
- Post-discharge follow-up to arrange appropriate injections/epinephrine management and ongoing allergy plan.

Quality checks (document quality):
- Missing elements: Vitals (no vitals documented); comprehensive meds reconciliation (only Salbutamol noted); full allergy severity details not documented.
- Internal conflicts: None identified.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some informal/redundant phrasing; no critical data omitted, but lacks objective exam findings and vitals.
